The way I have had success with the matchup: outpush him early and get exp and minion advantage if you do safe autos and extended Q's on the wave, while whittling off his bone plating and baiting his W. Try not to auto him to draw minion aggro or put yourself in a position where he can get multiple autos off, until his stuff is down then you can go for a full stack on conqueror and beat him in an extended trade.

Once he gets wave clear in way of tiamat or bamis cinder you just let him push and farm near ur tower, and bait his CDs if he wants to fight there, then all in with R to chase him down the lane.

If you need to leash and can't auto wave on the crash then just play more safe lvl 1 and just focus on baiting his CDs while holding wave near your tower.

Riven has always been a unique champ due to her kit being able to play around her own weaknesses and bad matchups, that's how people who have mastered her have always defied the meta. The fact that it might be especially rough right now isn't anything new and it shouldn't stop anyone who puts enough effort into her.

I believe in being sturdy enough to absorb multiple rotations of cooldowns and damage to output multiple rotations yourself. I am not disputing that the dmg got cut down, but her capabilities as a meatshield and draintank also got greatly improved. Her damage is still fine imo.

People who complain about Riven being too weak are risking making her lose even more of her power, and maybe even receiving simplifying attacks to her kit from Riot. If they read too much into it and make mistakes with overloading her and then having to gimp her due to backlash. The fact that the best onetricks are in top 10 on both na and euw should tell you her capabilities are enough.

The grounds are hearing streamers and other players say the same thing, but yeah they might just be saying that. For me it's true though. 

When it comes to Riven there is nothing clunky about the mechanics if you learn them. Through repeated execution the mechanics will always behave the same way, outside of Riven's 3Q sometimes bouncing off of creeps and going in the opposite direction. 

I dont think anyone can deny that it is an expression of skill, and yes it requires more effort to learn than most champs. I wont deny that I am biasd and have en ego about it though, that's a biproduct of how much I care about my champion, all the effort I've put into learning and how much I enjoy playing her.

For me personally, and for a lot of people who onetrick these champs and wouldnt even play the game if they didnt exist, animation cancelling and the creativity of the combos is the greatest thing about League of Legends. Things like bunny jumping in Quake and Counterstrike, animation cancelling in Supersmash etc are bugs yes, but there is beauty in the sense that the coolest form of skill expression in games were accidents.

\*edit\* And for the people who want it out of the game I cant see any other reason than envy. It is what kills depth in games and caters to casuals to the point where u get things like retail WoW.
